claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! It's lovely to meet you. Let me ask a few questions about Alex and your situation to determine your eligibility.

First, could you tell me: are you responsible for Alex? This could mean he lives with you, or you contribute to the cost of looking after him at least the same amount as Child Benefit would be.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm responsible for Alex. He lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

Next, could you tell me where you live? Specifically, are you living in the UK (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Lovely, thank you. Manchester is a great city!

One more question: is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, yes - his other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for him. They live with us too.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. That's an important detail.

Under the Child Benefit rules, only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any one time. Since Alex's other parent is already receiving Child Benefit for him, you wouldn't be able to make a separate claim for Alex while that existing claim is active.

However, if circumstances change (for example, if the other parent stops their claim), you could then make a claim yourself.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit, or were you perhaps looking to take over the claim from Alex's other parent?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. So because they're already claiming it, I can't claim it myself right now? That makes sense. No, I wasn't looking to take over the claim - I just wanted to check if I was eligible. Thank you for explaining that to me!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! Yes, you've understood correctly – since Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you're not able to make a separate claim at this time.

Let me now provide you with my formal assessment of your eligibility:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Here's a summary of my assessment:

**Child Benefit Eligibility for Alex: Not Eligible**

**Reason:** While you meet the general criteria for claiming Child Benefit (you're responsible for Alex, he lives with you, he's under 16, and you live in the UK), only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any one time. Since Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you cannot make a separate claim.

If anything changes in the future – for example, if the other parent decides to stop their claim – you would then be able to apply.

Thank you for chatting with me today, and I hope this has been helpful! If you have any other questions in the future, feel free to ask. 😊
